result.summary: The pedestrian environment is situated beneath an elevated rail structure, which creates significant visual obstructions due to large steel support columns. While sidewalks are present, the lack of marked crossings and the dark, enclosed nature of the space under the tracks reduce overall pedestrian safety and comfort.

hazards.name: Structural Columns
hazards.description: Large steel columns supporting the elevated rail are positioned at the curb, obstructing sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curb lines throughout the visible block.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible crosswalks or pedestrian infrastructure to facilitate safe crossing of the two-way roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility continental crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions (bulb-outs) at potential crossing points to improve visibility around the structural columns and reduce crossing distance.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting specifically directed at the sidewalks and crossing areas to mitigate the shadows cast by the overhead structure.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a continuous sidewalk directly abutting a commercial frontage, though it lacks a protective buffer from the adjacent roadway. Metal barricades and closed security shutters create a somewhat enclosed and inactive streetscape, while the pavement shows signs of wear.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle separation
hazards.description: There is no physical buffer or planting strip between the sidewalk and the travel lanes.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstructions
hazards.description: Metal barricades are placed on the sidewalk, narrowing the effective walking width.
hazards.location_in_image: In front of the pawn shop

hazards.name: Uneven pavement
hazards.description: The sidewalk surface shows signs of wear and unevenness, which could be a trip hazard.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground sidewalk area

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Introduce a buffer zone with street trees or planters to separate pedestrians from moving traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair
interventions.description: Resurface the sidewalk to provide a smooth, accessible path for all users.

interventions.title: Remove unnecessary barricades
interventions.description: Clear the sidewalk of temporary metal fencing to maximize the clear walking width.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by an overhead rail structure that creates deep shadows and significant visual obstructions via its support pillars. While sidewalks are continuous and a bike lane is present, the lack of physical protection and poor sightlines at the curb edge create a moderately hostile environment for non-motorized users.

hazards.name: Elevated Rail Pillars
hazards.description: Large steel pillars at the curb line create significant blind spots, hiding pedestrians from approaching traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curb lines supporting the overhead structure

hazards.name: Unprotected Bike Lane
hazards.description: The bike lane is only separated from vehicle traffic by a painted line, providing no physical safety for cyclists.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the roadway

hazards.name: Poor Visibility due to Shadows
hazards.description: The overhead structure blocks natural light, creating a dim environment that reduces the conspicuity of pedestrians and cyclists.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire roadway and sidewalk area beneath the structure

interventions.title: Under-deck Lighting
interventions.description: Install bright, pedestrian-scaled lighting on the underside of the elevated structure to eliminate dark spots and improve safety.

interventions.title: Protected Bike Lane
interventions.description: Install physical barriers such as flex-posts or concrete curbs to separate the bike lane from the travel lane.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Build out the sidewalk at intersections to move pedestrians past the line of pillars before they cross, improving sightlines.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a wide roadway under an elevated structure, with a sidewalk that is fenced off by metal barriers. The adjacent building features a long, blank frontage with closed shutters, contributing to a lack of natural surveillance and a desolate atmosphere.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Barriers
hazards.description: Metal crowd-control style barriers line the sidewalk edge, which can restrict pedestrian movement and prevent safe egress from the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the edge of the sidewalk in front of the striped building.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The long stretch of closed shutters and a windowless wall reduces natural surveillance and makes the environment feel isolated.
hazards.location_in_image: The building facade on the left side of the image.

interventions.title: Midblock Pedestrian Crossing
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with appropriate signage to provide a safe crossing point across the wide roadway.

interventions.title: Street Lighting Improvements
interventions.description: Enhance lighting under the elevated structure to improve visibility and perceived safety for pedestrians at night.

interventions.title: Frontage Activation
interventions.description: Encourage active ground-floor uses or install public art/murals to improve the pedestrian experience and increase 'eyes on the street'.
